plugins.//: 🎨 REPLACE: say what YOUR app does with photos, the camera and the microphone, with an example (Apple 5.1.1). iOS keeps all three strings: the picker's code can ask for each. Android declares only what the app uses: picking photos needs no permission (the system photo picker), so storage stays blocked; unblock CAMERA (and RECORD_AUDIO for video) in android.blockedPermissions when a screen calls launchCameraAsync.
plugins.photosPermission: $(PRODUCT_NAME) opens your photo library when you pick a photo to upload, like a profile picture. Only the photos you pick are shared with the app.
plugins.cameraPermission: $(PRODUCT_NAME) uses your camera when you choose to take a photo to upload, like a profile picture.
plugins.microphonePermission: $(PRODUCT_NAME) listens while you hold the mic to talk to your pet, and records sound while you film a video to upload.

plugins.//: Talking to the pet (M6): what you say becomes text on the phone. The microphone string is the app's one NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, so it is the same in every plugin that sets it (expo-image-picker, expo-audio) and covers both uses.
plugins.microphonePermission: $(PRODUCT_NAME) listens while you hold the mic to talk to your pet, and records sound while you film a video to upload.
plugins.speechRecognitionPermission: $(PRODUCT_NAME) turns what you say to your pet into text, so your pet can answer you. Recordings are never kept.

plugins.//: Only plays the pet's short sounds: no recording, and no background audio (App Review questions an audio background mode the app doesn't need).
plugins.microphonePermission: $(PRODUCT_NAME) listens while you hold the mic to talk to your pet, and records sound while you film a video to upload.

plugins.//: Tilting the phone moves the pet a little (v3 pet looks, R17): the accelerometer only, which needs no permission. Motion permission is off, so the pedometer's code is compiled out, the app can never ask for Motion & Fitness, and there is no purpose string to write.

expo-notifications, applied by our plugin so it can remove the push entitlement afterwards: the pet's daily note is a local notification, scheduled on the phone (v2-notifications R1), with the system sound and the app icon. A free Apple account can't sign push.
